subject: URGENT: ForgePoint production — sustained latency and 5xx surge in eu-west-2
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@forgepoint.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@forgepoint.com
Date: 2028-06-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: High error rates and timeouts - EU-WEST-2

Vanessa,

We're seeing a progressive failure in our production traffic routed through eu-west-2 starting ~08:55 UTC — 20-40% of requests are returning 500/504s and median p99 latency has climbed from ~210ms to >3s. This is affecting our checkout flow (payment authorization).

We've attached a trace dump and a couple of sample request IDs. Our customers are experiencing timeouts and the Ops team is getting paged. Can Redwood confirm whether there's an ongoing regional issue or whether this is on our end? We need immediate mitigation — if you can reroute traffic or advise a safe failover path, we will follow.

Trace: trace_dump_0618.zip (attached)
Sample request IDs: f7e3a1, b9d2c4

Please escalate.

—Alex
Head of Ops, ForgePoint
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:18:00Z
Subject: Fwd: High error rates and timeouts - EU-WEST-2

Team — forwarding ForgePoint outage. They report large 5xx surge + p99 latency blowup in eu-west-2 and need immediate mitigation.

Ask: can SRE assess whether this maps to our regional capacity / routing or customer-side request patterns? If we can flip their routing to eu-west-1 (or apply a route override) with minimal disruption, flag the risk and ETA. Soojin, please lead comms and keep me posted every 15 minutes. Hannah, can you validate whether kv-cache saturation or backend flapping shows up in our metrics?

I will loop in leadership if we need to change routing policy for this customer (impact to circuit breaker behavior for shared pools).

Thanks,
Vanessa
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: High error rates and timeouts - EU-WEST-2

On Tue, Jun 18, 2028 at 09:18 Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> Team — forwarding ForgePoint outage.

Checked ForgePoint's token-level trace and the customer-supplied dumps. Early signs: sustained token backpressure and a rising 5xx ratio originating from a small subset of model variants they pin to. Dashboard snapshot: error rate jumping from 1.2% to 28% over 20m; KV cache eviction spikes correlate with the error window.

Immediate options:
- Option A (low blast): enable prefix KVCACHE bypass for ForgePoint (reduce cache pressure) + throttle burst QPS to 70% for 10m — non-invasive but may not fully recover checkout latency.
- Option B (higher impact): apply a routing override to send their traffic to eu-west-1 (compatible instance family) — expected user-facing interruption ~10-30s during DNS/rewrite propagation; full traffic shift ~6–12 minutes.

I'll prepare the customer-facing note and coordinate with SRE. If SRE needs an exec sign-off for cross-region override (policy change), we'll surface immediately.

—Soojin
Senior Customer Success Manager
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:49:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: High error rates and timeouts - EU-WEST-2

On Tue, Jun 18, 2028 at 09:34 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Dashboard snapshot: error rate jumping ... KV cache eviction spikes correlate with the error window.

SRE update (summary):
- Observed: control-plane logs show persistent allocation churn in eu-west-2 hostgroup a-3 between 08:47-09:25 UTC. Node OOM-like churn coincides with high mempressure in the seq-attention kernel path for specific quantized model variant (v3q).
- Impact: sustained P50->P99 tail amplification, and transient 502/504s from upstream proxies when hostgroup drained.

Recommended immediate runbook (we can execute now):
1) Apply customer-specific routing override to divert 100% of ForgePoint traffic from eu-west-2 to eu-west-1 using emergency-routing flag (redwood:route_override=forgepoint_fp7421).
2) Spin up two warm workers in eu-west-1 pre-warmed for the pinned model variant.
3) Monitor for error rate reduction and latency improvement (target p99 < 500ms within 12 minutes).
4) If errors persist, rollback to eu-west-2 and run a controlled cache-bust and model restart.

Notes: cross-region override modifies routing policy and will temporarily bypass multi-tenant bursting protections. That means a potential resource impact on eu-west-1; we estimate low risk given current capacity. I'll attach the step-by-step doc.

Attachment: cross_region_reroute_steps.md

ETA to complete step 1–2: 8–12 minutes after sign-off.

—Hannah
Principal SRE
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:57:00Z
Subject: Request: Emergency cross-region override approval for ForgePoint (FP-7421)

Sean — quick ask. ForgePoint (FP-7421) is experiencing a production outage in eu-west-2 (high 5xx and p99 latency). SRE recommends an emergency routing override to shift their traffic to eu-west-1; estimated completion 8–12 minutes and expected to restore checkout since the issue appears tied to v3q model variant capacity/eviction behavior.

Risk: temporary bypass of shared bursting protections for a single customer (low probability of impacting eu-west-1 capacity). Proposed customer concession: 15% credit for the incident window.

I need a quick approval to proceed with the cross-region override and to confirm the credit offer. If approved, I'll send the technical ETA to ForgePoint and kick off the reroute.

TL;DR: Approve emergency reroute + 15% AM credit?

—Vanessa
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Emergency cross-region override approval for ForgePoint (FP-7421)

Approved. Execute the routing override and the warm worker spin-up. Approve 15% credit for the affected billing window and open an incident postmortem with SRE/CS/Product. I want a timeline of actions and a short customer-facing explanation once this is complete — keep it factual and avoid implementation details.

Please confirm once traffic has fully shifted and errors are reduced.

—Sean
VP, Customer Operations
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@forgepoint.com>, ForgePoint Ops <ops@forgepoint.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T10:11:00Z
Subject: Action taken: emergency routing override — ForgePoint (FP-7421)

Alex — update from Redwood: we executed an emergency cross-region routing override at 10:05 UTC and shifted ForgePoint traffic from eu-west-2 to eu-west-1. Hannah's team pre-warmed workers for the pinned model variant. Early metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 28% -> 1.8% and p99 latency improved to ~420ms within ~9 minutes of the action.

What we did:
- Applied route_override (redwood:route_override=forgepoint_fp7421) at 10:05 UTC.
- Warmed two dedicated workers in eu-west-1 to handle pinned model variant.
- Monitoring in progress; SRE will hold until we see sustained stability for 1 hour.

Compensation: Redwood will issue a 15% credit for the incident window as a gesture of goodwill; I will follow up with your billing contact to finalize.

Next steps:
1) SRE will continue monitoring and keep you updated every 30 minutes for the next hour.
2) We will schedule a postmortem and a plan to avoid recurrence (model variant pinning + quantized path stress testing).

Appreciate your patience — please escalate any immediate regressions.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: cross_region_reroute_steps.md
